verses.1: Then Job added another parable and spoke:
verses.2: Oh, that I were as in previous months, as in the days when God watched over me!
verses.3: When His lamp shone over my head, and in His light I walked through darkness.
verses.4: When I was in the fullness of my days, and God kept watch over my tent.
verses.5: When the Almighty was still with me, and my children were around me.
verses.6: When I went out to wash my steps in the heat, and the stone would yield fatness to me.
verses.7: When I stepped out at dawn into the gate, and in the street I set up my seat.
verses.8: The young men saw me and hid, and the elders would rise up.
verses.9: The leaders would hold back their words, and place their hand over their mouth.
verses.10: The voices of rulers would be silent, and their tongues would stick to their jaws.
verses.11: For the ear that heard me would bless me, and the eye that saw me would give me witness.
verses.12: For I rescued the poor who cried out, and the orphan who had no helper.
verses.13: The blessing of the one who was lost would come upon me, and the heart of a widow I would comfort.
verses.14: I clothed myself with righteousness and it covered me as a robe; my judgment was a crown.
verses.15: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the one who stumbled.
verses.16: I was a father to the poor, and I investigated a case I did not know.
verses.17: I would crush the grinding teeth of the wicked, and pluck the prey from their jaws.
verses.18: I said, “My strength will grow old, like a date palm, I will live many days.”
verses.19: My roots were spread toward water, and dew would rest on my harvest.
verses.20: My glory was renewed with me, and my bow was in my hand, it would change.
verses.21: To me they listened and waited, and in silence they took in my counsel.
verses.22: They did not contradict my words, and when I spoke to them, they were delighted.
verses.23: They would wait for me as the ground longs for the rain, and their mouths would open as for a storm.
verses.24: If I laughed at them, they would not believe; and the light of my face would not fall on them.
verses.25: I chose their way, and I sat as a leader. I dwelled as a king among troops, like one who comforts mourners.

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "the Almighty" (shaddai) is a common title for God in poetic contexts, rendered here in a way that reflects its role as a divine name.
- v. 6: "fatness" refers to the richness or abundance of the stone, likely metaphorical, as stones do not yield fat literally.
- v. 20: "my bow was in my hand, it would change" is a difficult line. "Change" is a possible rendering of "yachalif," but the exact meaning is ambiguous.
- v. 25: "as a king among troops" reflects the imagery of "g'dud," which can mean "army" or "group." The phrase "like one who comforts mourners" interprets the poetic parallel.

[1] Then Job added another parable and spoke:

[2] Oh, that I were as in previous months, as in the days when God watched over me!

[3] When His lamp shone over my head, and in His light I walked through darkness.

[4] When I was in the fullness of my days, and God kept watch over my tent.

[5] When the Almighty was still with me, and my children were around me.

[6] When I went out to wash my steps in the heat, and the stone would yield fatness to me.

[7] When I stepped out at dawn into the gate, and in the street I set up my seat.

[8] The young men saw me and hid, and the elders would rise up.

[9] The leaders would hold back their words, and place their hand over their mouth.

[10] The voices of rulers would be silent, and their tongues would stick to their jaws.

[11] For the ear that heard me would bless me, and the eye that saw me would give me witness.

[12] For I rescued the poor who cried out, and the orphan who had no helper.

[13] The blessing of the one who was lost would come upon me, and the heart of a widow I would comfort.

[14] I clothed myself with righteousness and it covered me as a robe; my judgment was a crown.

[15] I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the one who stumbled.

[16] I was a father to the poor, and I investigated a case I did not know.

[17] I would crush the grinding teeth of the wicked, and pluck the prey from their jaws.

[18] I said, “My strength will grow old, like a date palm, I will live many days.”

[19] My roots were spread toward water, and dew would rest on my harvest.

[20] My glory was renewed with me, and my bow was in my hand, it would change.

[21] To me they listened and waited, and in silence they took in my counsel.

[22] They did not contradict my words, and when I spoke to them, they were delighted.

[23] They would wait for me as the ground longs for the rain, and their mouths would open as for a storm.

[24] If I laughed at them, they would not believe; and the light of my face would not fall on them.

[25] I chose their way, and I sat as a leader. I dwelled as a king among troops, like one who comforts mourners.
